summary: A here document (<< EOF) feeds several lines of text to a command, right from your script. Use it to print a block of text, write a file, or give input to a command without a separate file.
notes: The ending marker must be alone on its line with nothing before or after it, not even spaces. EOF is a tradition; any word works.
With << 'EOF' in quotes, bash does not fill in $5 or $name, so the text prints exactly as written.
<<- only removes tab characters. If your editor turns tabs into spaces, the EOF line is not found.
pitfall: If the closing EOF is indented with spaces or misspelled, bash reads to the end of the file and warns here-document at line 8 delimited by end-of-file (wanted `EOF'). Everything after it becomes text instead of commands.
